metadata.author: transcribed from live/runs by expansion agent
metadata.key_test: Safeguard B (capacity gate): a low fragment count (2 successors) is NOT manageable when P1 sits below the bottom-third WGI Rule of Law. Also tests Safeguard E (rentier capture) bidirectionally.
metadata.notes: Pillar scores are derived ordinal/estimated values, not direct WGI extraction. Sudan WGI given on 0-100 absolute scale; South Sudan has a near-total pre-2011 governance-data vacuum treated as signal, never interpolated.

pre_event.event_description: Unified Sudan -> South Sudan independence referendum and secession (July 9, 2011); secondary fragmentation in South Sudan civil war (Dec 2013).

context.neighbor_details: Sudan and South Sudan as mutual predatory neighbors (Abyei, Heglig 2012, oil-transit chokehold).

Sudan.notes: WGI shown on 0-100 absolute scale (Sudan scored well below 10 in all governance areas in 2010 per World Bank WGI - functionally floor-level). Legacy-scale government-effectiveness estimate ~ -1.3 (1996 high -0.987, 2014 low -1.532). TI CPI 2011 = 1.6/10 (177/183). Derived pillar estimate: P1 approx 0.06 (floor), P4 severely distorted by oil + ODA, P5 approx floor (Darfur); estimated MI low/floor tier. Pillar spread narrow but uniformly catastrophic (dangerous 'uniform low' profile).

context.admin_details: Heavy UN/donor presence (UNMISS); measured capacity partly reflects external actors (Safeguard A flag).
context.neighbor_details: Mutual predatory dynamic with Sudan (Abyei, Heglig, oil-transit).

South Sudan.notes: No prior independent statehood; literacy ~34.5%; oil = ~98% of government budget and ~80% of GDP; oil rents peaked at 58.3% of GDP in 2008. Derived pillar estimate: P1 approx 0.02-0.04 (world floor), P2 floor, P3 floor (literacy), P4 extreme rentier distortion, P5 floor; estimated MI bottom of dataset. The near-total absence of independent governance statistics pre-2011 is itself the signal of institutional vacuum - reported as missing, never interpolated.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Sudan (north) marginally better trajectory than South Sudan (higher P1).
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: P1 ordinality; Sudan marginally above South Sudan's world-floor P1.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: South Sudan matches or exceeds Sudan's trajectory.

b_violence.prediction: Violent outcome predicted for both successor states.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Either state remains peaceful and stable.

c_convergence.basis: Both units at uniform floor P1.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: One state diverges upward to a stable trajectory.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: South Sudan fails on institutional vacuum (P1) compounded by rentier distortion (P4/E); Sudan fails on P1 + P5.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Failure driven by an unrelated dimension.

e_fragment_count.prediction: Fragment count is 2, but Safeguard B implies catastrophe regardless of low count.
e_fragment_count.falsification_condition: Low fragment count yields a manageable, non-catastrophic outcome.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: South Sudan reversal/non-delivery PROBABLE (new state, oil rents >30% GDP, ODA dependence, no delivery capacity).
f_reversal_risk.falsification_condition: South Sudan consolidates and delivers governance.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: The 2010 floor-P1 profile predicts South Sudan's 2013 secondary fragmentation; no functioning suppression-vs-prevention apparatus (Tier 1 / below).

Sudan.outcome_summary: FSI 2024 = 109.3 (2nd most fragile globally). Civil war since April 15, 2023 (SAF vs RSF); ~11-12M displaced (world's largest displacement crisis); famine confirmed Aug 1, 2024 (Zamzam camp).

South Sudan.outcome_summary: FSI 2024 = 109.0 (3rd most fragile); HDI 2023 = 0.388 (193rd, last in world). Civil war Dec 2013-2018 with ~383,000 deaths (LSHTM study, ~190,000 direct violent); GDP per capita fell from ~$1,400 (2011) to under $500; near-renewed war 2025.

a_trajectory.evidence: Sudan 109.3 vs South Sudan 109.0 on FSI - statistically indistinguishable.
a_trajectory.explanation: Ordinal claim barely holds; both went catastrophic, so the marginal ranking is not discriminating at the floor. [run6 §4 Mod4: pre-event P1 gap within the WGI margin of error -> 'too close to call'; coded PARTIAL, not CONFIRMED.]

b_violence.evidence: Both states experienced mass-casualty war (Sudan 2023-; South Sudan 2013-2018).
b_violence.explanation: Low-floor P1 in both successors -> violent breakdown as predicted.

c_convergence.evidence: Convergence at the floor (FSI ~109 for both).
c_convergence.explanation: Both units collapsed to the catastrophic floor.

d_failure_dimension.evidence: World Bank: oil 'contributes 60 percent of GDP, 99 percent of exports and 85 percent of government revenues' yet 'Nine out of ten people live below the poverty line'; per capita GDP fell 76%.
d_failure_dimension.explanation: Failure dimensions matched: South Sudan institutional vacuum + rentier distortion; Sudan P1+P5. [STRICT RE-CODE per run6 §3(d): post-hoc 'primary dimension' identification invites confirmation bias; coded PARTIAL under strict standards.]

e_fragment_count.explanation: Safeguard B vindicated: fragment count is meaningless below the capacity gate.

f_reversal_risk.explanation: South Sudan never delivered governance; reversal as predicted.

g_suppression.evidence: Secondary fragmentation (2013 civil war) predicted by the 2010 floor-P1 profile.
g_suppression.explanation: Floor-P1 profile anticipated South Sudan's secondary fragmentation within 29 months of independence.

h_turbulence.explanation: No high-P1 survivor; substate-turbulence prediction not made for this case.

result_coding_reference.CONFIRMED: Prediction matched outcome on the specific dimension predicted
result_coding_reference.PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: Direction correct but magnitude, form, or timing significantly different
result_coding_reference.NOT_APPLICABLE: Prediction type not relevant to this case

analysis.overall_assessment: 7 applicable predictions: 6 CONFIRMED, 1 PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED (a), 0 FALSIFIED. The framework's strongest demonstration of Safeguard B.
safeguards_triggered: Safeguard B (capacity gate) - TRIGGERED maximally: 2 successors but P1 far below bottom-third Rule of Law -> catastrophe regardless of low fragment count
Safeguard E (rentier capture) - TRIGGERED bidirectionally: oil bought initial elite cohesion then became the mechanism of collapse when factional distribution broke down (2013)
Safeguard D (predatory neighbor) - TRIGGERED (mutual predation Sudan/South Sudan)
Safeguard A (external admin) - partial flag (heavy UN/donor presence)
new_failure_modes_discovered: Floor compression: P1 loses discriminating power when both units sit below the capacity gate.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Fragment count is meaningless below the capacity gate (Safeguard B), and Safeguard E appears in full bidirectional form: oil first bought cohesion (more durable than P1 predicts at independence), then the rentier system became the mechanism of collapse.
proposed_framework_modifications: Promote Safeguard B to primary status for low-count fragmentations: when P1 < bottom-third WGI Rule of Law, score 'catastrophic regardless of fragment count' before consulting P1 ordinality.
analysis.baseline_impact: Reinforces existing safeguards; Safeguard B promotion is a candidate refinement, not a degradation of the 20-case baseline.
analysis.strict_recode_note: Strict re-code applied per run6 (post-hoc d-dimension -> PARTIAL; narrow-gap a-trajectory annotated with Mod4). Honest aggregate target ~62-78%.
